title: Strait Is the Way, the Door Is Strait
description: Strait Is the Way, the Door Is Strait in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 11 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 161, headed “Christian virtues; or, The difficulty of conversion”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Strait is the way, the door is strait That leads to joys on high; 'Tis but a few that find the gate, While crowds mis-take and die.

lines: Strait is the way, the door is strait
That leads to joys on high;
'Tis but a few that find the gate,
Flesh is a dangerous foe to grace,
Flesh must be humbled, pride abas'd,
The love of gold be banish'd hence,
The tongue, that most unruly power,
We must be watchful every hour,
Lord, can a feeble helpless worm
Thy grace must all my work perform,
My thoughts surmount these lower skies
There springs of endless pleasure rise,
There I behold with sweet delight
And strong affections fix my sight
His promise stands for ever firm,
He binds my name upon his arm,
And seals it on his heart.
Light are the pains that' nature brings,
I would not be a stranger still
Where I for ever hope to dwell

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
